Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0024-reverse-75", "row_sha256": "3df05135ae6da7b4c462615bbd16d25c7b53079f0ad1eabfae846f32d945283c", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
please turn this into a proper request for a fictional dye log entry, not the entry itself. it should be one new, self-contained episode in an english textile dye log, and it needs to read like a working record rather than a story. keep the details below in it but put them in an order a dyer or supervisor can follow. the entry is for the wednesday 14 may 2025 shift, shift b, in dye room bay 2. the shift ran 06:40 to 14:20. this isn't meant to revise some earlier incident, it's its own event. the record concerns vat d-17 and lot tw-508, which was 36 kg of greige yarn in a 70 percent wool and 30 percent linen blend. the job was to dye it slate blue. don't turn the request into a general procedure for dyeing other lots, and don't make up missing readings or decisions.

start with the lot and equipment information, then move into what happened during the shift. the recipe card called for 540 g of direct blue 86, 180 g of sodium sulfate, and 72 g of sodium carbonate. the additions were weighed separately on scale s-4; its check weight was recorded as passing at 06:52. note that this is what the card called for, not a claim that the recipe was independently checked or changed. the bath fill began at 06:45, the yarn was loaded at 06:58, and the run began at 07:05. the bath reached 42 c at 07:31, then rose to 78 c by 08:16. it was held at 78 c until the operator stopped circulation at 11:18 to inspect the return-line filter. don't describe that stop as a breakdown or say it was caused by a blockage; all that's known is that the filter was inspected. circulation resumed at 11:42, and the bath was drained at 13:56. the rinse was recorded at 14:12, before the shift ended.

include measurements as measurements and don't smooth out their differences. ph was 6.8 at 07:02, 7.1 at 08:20, and 7.0 at 11:10. the temperature display and the handheld probe both showed 78 c at 08:16, but the handheld probe read 77 c at 10:05 while the display stayed at 78 c. the log doesn't say which reading was right, so leave that unresolved rather than choosing one. at 09:40 the operator took a small swatch from the sample loop. it looked slate blue under the room lights, although a narrow lighter band was visible along one edge when it was held near the inspection lamp. Mara, the operator, said, “The blue is still holding at the edge.” keep that as her comment, not a confirmed assessment of the whole batch. a second swatch was taken at 12:05 after circulation resumed; its note says “similar shade; edge still lighter.” don't claim that the second swatch passed or that the band disappeared.

make the sequence legible, perhaps with a numbered section for the shift observations if that fits the format, but don't make the whole piece a checklist if short paragraphs would work better. there was no entry on the sheet naming a cause for the lighter edge. no corrective addition, re-dye, or second recipe was recorded, so don't invent one or imply that anything like that happened. the card's stated target was slate blue; the notes describe what the samples looked like, and those aren't the same thing as an approval. say plainly that the record contains no release decision and no sign-off. keep the status open at the end of the recorded facts, without deciding whether the lot was acceptable, rejected, or awaiting a particular person. avoid adding a resolution just to give the episode an ending.

include the ordinary handling details that connect the observations: the yarn stayed in vat d-17 during the inspection stop, no change of lot was written down, and the shift sheet identifies Mara as the operator. don't add a supervisor's name, a second operator, a customer, a deadline, or a reason the work was scheduled. the record does not say whether the filter was clean, whether the sample was checked against a standard under another light, or whether the pH readings prompted an action. leave those gaps as gaps rather than turning them into findings. use the times as recorded and retain the distinction between the run starting at 07:05 and the bath fill starting at 06:45.

write it in a neutral, practical voice with enough detail that someone reading the log can trace the run without needing a dramatic explanation. keep the quote exactly as given and identify Mara as its speaker. use the vat and lot labels in a consistent form, and retain the blend, quantities, temperatures, and times. don't add a conclusion, approval, recommendation, or account of what happened after the rinse. send the finished entry to Leonie, not Ellis. the final paragraph should contain distinct record information rather than repeat the earlier chronology: include that the shift sheet ends at 14:20, the operator is listed as Mara, and no release decision or sign-off appears on this record. that is all that is known for the closing note.", "output": "Please write one self-contained, fictional English textile dye log entry for a new episode. It should read like a practical working record, not a story or a general dyeing procedure. Organize the supplied facts in a clear sequence that a dyer or supervisor can follow. Do not add readings, events, or decisions that are not listed here.

**Record details**

The record is for Wednesday, 14 May 2025, shift B, in dye room bay 2. The shift ran from 06:40 to 14:20. It concerns vat D-17 and lot TW-508: 36 kg of greige yarn in a blend of 70 percent wool and 30 percent linen. The target color on the recipe card was slate blue.

The card called for 540 g of direct blue 86, 180 g of sodium sulfate, and 72 g of sodium carbonate. The additions were weighed separately on scale S-4. Its check weight was recorded as passing at 06:52. Present these as the card’s recipe and the recorded scale check; do not imply that the recipe was independently checked or changed.

**Shift chronology and observations**

1. The bath fill began at 06:45, the yarn was loaded at 06:58, and the run began at 07:05. Keep the fill time distinct from the run start.
2. The bath reached 42 C at 07:31 and 78 C by 08:16. It was held at 78 C until circulation was stopped at 11:18 for an inspection of the return-line filter. The yarn remained in vat D-17 during the stop. Circulation resumed at 11:42, the bath was drained at 13:56, and the rinse was recorded at 14:12.
3. Record the pH measurements individually: 6.8 at 07:02, 7.1 at 08:20, and 7.0 at 11:10. At 08:16, both the temperature display and handheld probe showed 78 C. At 10:05, the handheld probe read 77 C while the display remained at 78 C. The record does not identify which reading was correct, so leave the difference unresolved.
4. At 09:40, the operator took a small swatch from the sample loop. It looked slate blue under the room lights, with a narrow lighter band along one edge when held near the inspection lamp. Identify Mara as the operator and retain her comment exactly: “The blue is still holding at the edge.” Present this as Mara’s comment, not as a confirmed assessment of the batch. A second swatch, taken at 12:05 after circulation resumed, was noted as “similar shade; edge still lighter.” Do not say that it passed or that the band disappeared.

**Limits and closing information**

The sheet does not name a cause for the lighter edge. It records no corrective addition, re-dye, or second recipe. Do not invent any of these or imply that they occurred. The target color and the sample observations are separate facts; do not turn the sample descriptions into an approval. The record does not say whether the filter was clean, whether a sample was checked against a standard under another light, or whether any pH reading prompted action. Leave each of these matters unstated. No change of lot is written down. Do not add a supervisor, another operator, a customer, a deadline, or a reason the work was scheduled.

Use a neutral, practical voice and preserve the recorded times, quantities, temperatures, blend, and labels. Short paragraphs are suitable, with a numbered section for observations if useful. Keep the status open: the record contains no release decision or sign-off. Do not decide that the lot was acceptable, rejected, or awaiting anyone, and do not add a resolution or describe events after the rinse. Send the finished entry to Leonie, not Ellis.

End with a distinct paragraph noting that the shift sheet ends at 14:20, lists Mara as the operator, and contains no release decision or sign-off. Do not use that closing paragraph to repeat the chronology."}]
